quiz.q: What is a crate in Rust?
options: The unit Rust compiles — a package, either a runnable binary or a reusable library
quiz.explain: A crate is the compilation unit: a binary crate runs (has main), a library crate is used by other crates.

quiz.q: By default, an item inside a module is...
options: Private — only visible inside its own module
quiz.explain: Everything is private by default. You add `pub` to expose an item to code outside its module.

quiz.q: How do you call a function `parse` from inside a module named `parser`?
quiz.explain: You reach into a module with the `::` path separator: `parser::parse()`. A dot is for method calls and field access.

options: Brings a name into scope so you can type its short form
quiz.explain: `use` imports a name so you can refer to it directly, e.g. `use parser::parse;` then just `parse(...)`. It does not create a module.

flashcards.back: Binary crate has `main` and runs. Library crate has no main; it offers functions/types for other crates to use.

flashcards.front: What's the default visibility of items in a module?
flashcards.back: Private — visible only inside their own module. Add `pub` to expose them.

flashcards.front: How do you reach into a module?
flashcards.back: With `::` (the path separator): `parser::parse()`. A dot is for methods/fields, not modules.
`mod` declares a module (creates it or points at its file). `use` just shortens an existing name so you can type less.
